summary: The About text describes the broad idea of learning to reverse a noise process. The toy morphs a fixed noise cloud into a known duck in ten stages; its 50-to-0 counter is a visual scale, not 50 calculated denoising steps.

claims.claim: Diffusion generation uses a learned reverse noise process.
claims.how: The About text gives an introductory description of adding noise for training and reversing it to generate a picture.

sources.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
sources.says: A learned reverse process generates data from noise after training on a forward noise process.

claims.claim: The toy has ten visual stages while the counter goes from 50 to 0.
claims.how: The stage helper selects ten morph values and the actual display reports 50 minus five times the stage.

sources.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
sources.says: A learned reverse process generates data from noise after training on a forward noise process.

claims.note: The number on the counter is illustrative and does not count learned network evaluations.

claims.claim: The clearing duck is a prepared illustration of generation.
claims.how: The morph blends fixed particle positions toward a known duck. No model predicts the noise to remove.

sources.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
sources.says: A learned reverse process generates data from noise after training on a forward noise process.

simplified: The duck is supplied in advance and there is no denoising network, training objective, or sampled reverse process. Ten visual stages decrease the counter by five each time.
